caseStudy.title: LedgerSift
caseStudy.background:
LedgerSift uses a Python Service Bus worker to extract features from enterprise invoices. Each partner is a separate logical domain. One subscription receives invoices while another captures auditing events. The extraction worker publishes a size-limited result and commits a PostgreSQL processing marker; it cannot make the broker completion and PostgreSQL transaction atomic.

A Container Apps worker currently scales on HTTP request concurrency even though it has no ingress. The team wants a queue-driven worker that can scale down between submissions. The data store uses tenant-specific records and an Azure Managed Redis expiration policy to release cached inference details.

Investigators need a KQL query that preserves failed requests lacking dependency telemetry. A missing sampled dependency span must not remove the parent failure from the report.

exhibits.title: Ordering requirements
exhibits.code:
Business key: partnerId + invoiceId + version
Message receive mode: PeekLock
Process exit may occur after SQL COMMIT but before broker completion

exhibits.code:
AppRequests(OperationId, TimeGenerated, Success, Name)
AppDependencies(OperationId, TimeGenerated, Target)
